transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-13
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Singh (Head of Data - Lynx), Carlos Ruiz (VP Eng - Lynx), Priya Menon (Security Lead - Lynx)

[00:00:00] Jasmine: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm jasmine patiell with Redwood, and with me is ethan kim, our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:10] Dr. Maya: Good, thanks. maya here. we'll try and keep this tight, got a 1pm sync after.
[00:00:15] Carlos: hi all, carlos here. curious about the private hosting options, we have strong constraints around data residency and no internet egress for PHI.
[00:00:25] Priya: hey, priya. primary question from security is how network integration works — vpc peering, private endpoints, whether redwood needs public egress, stuff like that.
[00:00:35] Jasmine: totally, that's the agenda. we support hosted, dedicated, and private (vpc) — today's focus is private VPC deployment: networking patterns, peering, private endpoints, region constraints, and auth/KMS. ethan will walk us through the technical tradeoffs.
[00:00:50] Ethan: thanks. quick caveat: i'll be fairly high level first then we can deep-dive. for private we offer two primary patterns on AWS: 1) VPC peering/transit-gateway to our private control plane, and 2) private endpoints (aws privatelink) to connect to a customer-managed endpoint. both avoid public internet.
[00:01:10] Dr. Maya: can you explain the difference again, peering vs private link? we have multiple accounts and strict CIDR allocation.
[00:01:20] Ethan: sure. VPC peering/transit-gw gives L3 routing — your subnets route to our service VPC. simpler for low-latency and for internal communications, but requires non-overlapping CIDRs. Privatelink (interface endpoints) is L4 through ENIs and works even with overlapping cidrs because traffic goes via endpoints. tradeoff: privatelink can add some per-ENI cost and slightly more mgmt overhead, peering is usually cheaper per-byte.
[00:01:50] Carlos: we’re worried about CIDR overlap — our VPCs use 10.0.0.0/8 ranges across accounts. is privatelink the recommended path then?
[00:02:00] Ethan: often yes for overlapping networks. also if you need to expose a single service endpoint per region privatelink is clean. for high-throughput workloads and extremely low-latency SLOs, teams sometimes use dedicated peering + a transit-gw and plan the cidrs accordingly.
[00:02:20] Priya: do you support cross-region deployments? we have data residency in eu-west-1 and us-east-1, and we'd like inference to run in the eu region for EU patients.
[00:02:30] Jasmine: yes — we can deploy private control plane and inference clusters in customer-preferred regions. region availability map will be in the architecture doc we send. note: some model kernels and GPU SKUs vary by region which can impact latency and cost.
[00:02:50] Dr. Maya: kernel variance — is that pre-quantized models or runtime-level? we've seen mismatch in performance across regions.
[00:02:58] Ethan: runtime and hardware variations. same model family can be on different instance types (A100 vs H100 etc) depending on region, which changes perf characteristics. we advise a benchmark per region. we'll propose a small benchmark plan in the follow-up.
[00:03:15] Carlos: how about egress? our compliance says no data should egress to public internet. does your private option still egress for things like model updates or telemetry?
[00:03:25] Ethan: no public egress for inference traffic in private mode. control-plane communication can be routed through the private links. telemetry and metrics can be configured to push to your monitoring endpoints (or kept internal). model updates can be staged via private bucket or customer-managed object store; we support pulling images from S3 with a role and VPC endpoint so there's no internet egress.
[00:03:47] Priya: KMS integration — we use a customer-managed KMS key in AWS, do you support envelope encryption and HSM/KMS wrapping?
[00:03:55] Ethan: yes, we integrate with customer KMS for keys. we also support HSM-backed workflows for highest assurance. we can provide diagrams for key rotation and access control.
[00:04:05] Dr. Maya: network ACLs and security groups — who manages those on the redwood side for privatelink?
[00:04:12] Ethan: for privatelink, you create an interface endpoint in your account and control SGs there. for peering, we provide the peering connection and you'll update route tables/SGs. we typically provide a prescriptive checklist to avoid common mistakes (e.g., asymmetric routing, missing route propagation on TGW).
[00:04:30] Jasmine: quick interjection — a couple of common gotchas: overlapping cidrs (as mentioned), MTU/path issues with transit-gw, and also DNS — if you want to use internal names we can provide private hosted zone delegation instructions.
[00:04:45] Carlos: dns delegation — will that require changes to our Route53?
[00:04:50] Ethan: typically we create a delegated subzone and you add NS records in your zone to point to our private hosted zone; for privatelink we return an A/AAAA for the interface endpoint IP. some teams prefer to keep their own records and map the endpoint IPs — we'll include both options.
[00:05:05] Priya: SSO and RBAC — how do you integrate with our identity provider?
[00:05:10] Jasmine: we support SAML/SSO with IdP (Okta/Active Directory), role-based access, and audit logs. for private deployments, audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM via our forwarding or kept in a customer-managed storage.
[00:05:25] Dr. Maya: curious about latency numbers — for our use case we need sub-200ms p99 on generation for short prompts (<=256 tokens). is that achievable in private?
[00:05:35] Ethan: it's workload-dependent. with dedicated pools and regional placement you can hit those targets for many models. we'll propose a test profile: sample prompts, concurrency, and model variants; then run a benchmark on the dedicated cluster in your EU region.
[00:05:50] Carlos: what's the path for canary or fallback? we need graceful degradation if our primary region faces capacity issues.
[00:05:58] Jasmine: smart routing supports failover to another region or a hosted-compatible fallback. for strict data residency we can configure fallback to a region within permitted jurisdictions. failover policy is configurable in the rollout.
[00:06:15] Priya: compliance question — do you provide SOC 2 reports and penetration test evidence?
[00:06:20] Jasmine: yes, SOC 2 available; we'll attach the latest report and pen test summary in the follow-up pack.
[00:06:28] Dr. Maya: on connectivity we have dedicated appliances and use a partner for transit — are there any special requirements for transit-gw or SD-WAN?
[00:06:35] Ethan: we integrate fine with transit-gw, but you must ensure proper route propagation. with SD-WAN if traffic is hairpinned we sometimes see path MTU issues, so it's on the checklist. we'll include recommended MTU and keepalive settings.
[00:06:50] Carlos: licensing and pricing model — does private imply a minimum committed capacity?
[00:06:56] Jasmine: private often maps to our Dedicated or Private SKU; Dedicated has reserved capacity with monthly commits, Private (VPC) has options — you can do a pilot with a small reserved pool or a metered deployment depending on requirements. i'll include t-shirt sizing and an example commit table.
[00:07:15] Dr. Maya: what's the onboarding timeline? if we sign a pilot, how quickly can we go live?
[00:07:20] Jasmine: typical pilot is 4-6 weeks: network setup (peering/privatelink), credentialing/KMS, model onboarding, and a short benchmark. we'll aim for the shorter end if we have network info and IPs.
[00:07:33] Priya: do you require any ports open outbound from our VPC?
[00:07:37] Ethan: for privatelink none — it's all internal. for peering you need routes; if you want control-plane callbacks we can set them to use the privatelink or a specific egress path. we'll document exact ports (usually TLS 443) and IP ranges.
[00:07:52] Carlos: about data deletion and retention — how do you ensure customer data isn't persisted in the control plane?
[00:07:58] Jasmine: in private mode we offer configs to prevent logging of payloads, and retention windows are configurable. we can also provide a data flow diagram showing where ephemeral caches (KV cache) exist and how to disable persistent logs.
[00:08:12] Dr. Maya: slight tangent — you mentioned KV cache, we've seen references to K-V cash in a previous doc, can you clarify what that is?
[00:08:18] Ethan: haha that's a transcription artifact — KV cache is key-value cache for attention state; it's ephemeral per inference and can be isolated per tenant. it doesn't persist to disk unless you opt-in.
[00:08:30] (brief cross-talk)
[00:08:35] Jasmine: want to talk through a sample network diagram live? i can share screen but maybe better to send the architecture doc and then schedule deep dive.
[00:08:44] Priya: please send the doc, and also a network checklist. we'll want to validate with our network team.
[00:08:50] Ethan: noted. i will add a mock peering test scenario and a privatelink verification steps (create endpoint, verify SGs, check dns resolution).
[00:08:59] Carlos: sample checklist items for us: provide VPC IDs, CIDR ranges, route tables, TGW attachments, and contact for network ops.
[00:09:07] Jasmine: perfect — that's what we'll request.
[00:09:10] Dr. Maya: one more question — is there a managed option for model updates, or do we need to push new model artifacts?
[00:09:16] Ethan: we can manage updates through a private artifact pipeline; alternatively you can push to a customer-managed S3 and we pull with an IAM role. both supported.
[00:09:26] Priya: are audit logs immediate or eventual? we want near-real-time logs for access events.
[00:09:31] Ethan: we can stream audit events to your logging endpoint in near-real-time (few seconds) using Kinesis/CloudWatch or via syslog forwarders.
[00:09:40] Jasmine: ok i'm mindful of time, let's jump to recap and next steps.
[00:09:45] Jasmine: recap: primary ask is private VPC in eu-west-1 with no public egress, KMS integration, SAML SSO, and p99 latency goal ~200ms. action items — we'll send SOC2, architecture doc, pricing, and a benchmark plan.
[00:09:58] Priya: sounds good. we'll share CIDR ranges and the network ops contact by tomorrow.
[00:10:05] Dr. Maya: thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[00:10:08] Carlos: thanks all.
[00:10:10] Jasmine: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and let's schedule the infra deep dive for next week.
